### 3.1 Mehrangarh Fort (मेहरानगढ़ दुर्ग, Jodhpur)
- **Topography & Construction**: Founded on 12 May 1459 by **Rao Jodha** upon the sheer basaltic crest of **Chidiyatunk Hill (चिड़ियाटूंक)**.
- **Nomenclature**: *Mayuradhwaja Durg* (peacock-shaped), *Garh Chintamani*, *Bihangadh*.
- **Rudyard Kipling's Immortal Tribute**:
  > *"A palace that might have been built by Titans and colored by the morning sun, created by angels, fairies, and giants!"*
- **Historic Cannons Mounted on Ramparts**:
  - **Kilkila (किलकिला)**
  - **Shambhuban (शंभूबाण)**
  - **Gajni Khan (गsingle/गजनी खां)**
  - **Kadak Bijli (कड़क बिजली)**
  - **Nusrat (नुसरत)**, **Gubara (गुबार)**, **Dhudhani (धूड़धाणी)**, **Jamjama**.
- **Cultural Monuments**:
  - **Chamunda Mata Temple**: Consecrated by Rao Jodha; site of the tragic stampede on 30 September 2008 (investigated by the **Justice Jaswant Chopra Commission**).
  - **Palaces**: Moti Mahal (Sawai Raja Sur Singh), Phool Mahal (Abhai Singh), Sheesh Mahal, Daulat Khana.
  - **Chhatri of Dhan-Bhiw**: Memorial of brave warriors Kanka and Bhiw.

---

### 3.2 Junagarh Fort (जूनागढ़ दुर्ग, Bikaner) — "Zameen ka Zeewar"
- **Topography & Epithet**: A premier **Dhanvan / Bhu-Durg** constructed on level ground (rather than a mountain cliff), hence celebrated as **"Zameen ka Zeewar" (जमीन का जेवर — The Jewel of the Earth)**.
- **Builder**: Constructed between **1589 and 1594 CE** by **Maharaja Rai Singh**, under the supervision of prime minister **Karam Chand**, on the ancient foundation of *Bikaji ki Tekri*.
- **Suraj Pol & Elephant Statues**: At the Suraj Pol (main gateway), Rai Singh installed life-size stone statues of the celebrated heroes of the Third Sāka of Chittor: **Jaimal Rathore** and **Patta Sisodia**, mounted on elephants.
- **Rai Singh Prashasti**: Composed by Jain scholar **Muni Jaita**, inscribed on the Suraj Pol ramparts.
- **Palaces**:
  - **Anup Mahal**: Decorated with exquisite gold-leaf lacquer work (*Usta Art*); traditional site of the royal coronation of Bikaner rulers.
  - **Badal Mahal**: Ceilings painted with blue swirling clouds and lightning, symbolizing monsoon rains in the Thar desert.
  - **Ganga Niwas**: Constructed by Maharaja Ganga Singh using red carved sandstone.

---

### 3.3 Taragarh Fort (Ajmer) — "The Gibraltar of Rajasthan"
- **Topography & Origins**: Erected atop the steep **Beetli Hill (बीठली पहाड़ी)**, hence historically designated as **Garh Beetli (गढ़ बीठली)**.
- **Builder**: Built in 1113 CE by Chauhan King **Ajayraja**; renovated by Mewar Prince Prithviraj Sisodia ("Udna Rajkumar"), who renamed it **Taragarh** after his courageous wife, **Tara Bai**.
- **Bishop Heber's Verdict**: Renowned British traveler Bishop Heber described Taragarh as:
  > *"The Gibraltar of Rajasthan"* (राजस्थान का जिब्राल्टर).
- **Sacred Monuments & Bastions**:
  - **Dargah of Miran Saheb**: Shrine of Governor **Mir Syed Hussain Khing-Sawar (मीरान साहेब)**, who was martyred defending the fort in 1202 CE.
  - **Ghode ki Mazar (घोड़े की मजार)**: The only sacred equestrian tomb of a horse in Rajasthan.
  - **14 Monumental Bastions**: Including *Ghunghat Burj*, *Gugadi Burj*, *Phooti Burj*, and *Shringar Chavari Burj*.
  - **Chhatri of Prithviraj Chauhan III**: Modern national memorial.

---

### 3.4 Taragarh Fort (Bundi) — "The Star Fort"
- **Builder**: Constructed in **1354 CE** by **Rao Bar Singh Hada**.
- **Topography & Name**: Appears in the shape of a colossal gleaming star (*Tara*) when viewed from the valley below.
- **Rudyard Kipling's Verdict**: In stark contrast to Mehrangarh, Kipling remarked that Taragarh Bundi was:
  > *"Built by ghosts and spirits rather than mortal men!"*  
  > *(यह दुर्ग मानव द्वारा नहीं, प्रेतों द्वारा निर्मित लगता है।)*
- **Garbha Gunjan Cannon (गर्भ गुंजन तोप)**: Colossal bronze cannon mounted atop the Bhim Burj; legend holds that its thunderous detonation induced miscarriages in pregnant women, giving it the name *Garbha Gunjan*.
- **Chitrashala (चित्रशाला / रंगविलास)**: Constructed under Maharao Umed Singh; world-famous for its green and blue frescoes depicting hunting scenes, monsoons, and Radha-Krishna devotion.

---

### 3.5 Bhatner Fort (भटनेर दुर्ग, Hanumangarh) — The Northern Shield
- **Historical Seniority**: The **oldest surviving fort in Rajasthan**, constructed in the late 3rd century (c. 285 / 295 CE) by Bhati King **Bhupat Bhati** on the banks of the ancient Saraswati (Ghaggar) river.
- **Construction Material**: Constructed almost entirely of **unbaked sun-dried bricks**.
- **Maximum Foreign Invasions**: Withstood the highest number of foreign invasions across Rajasthan's history, defending northern trade routes against invaders from Ghazni, Kabul, and Multan (*Uttar Bhad Kivad*).
- **Timur's Invasion (1398 CE)**: Sultan Timur (Tamerlane) besieged Bhatner in 1398 CE. In his autobiography *Tuzuk-i-Timuri*, Timur recorded:
  > *"I have never seen a fortress so formidable, strong, and unyielding across the entirety of Hindustan as Bhatner!"*
  (During Timur's siege, Hindu and Muslim women performed **Jauhar together** inside Bhatner Fort).
- **Renaming to Hanumangarh (1805 CE)**: Recaptured by Maharaja Surat Singh of Bikaner on a **Tuesday (मंगलवार)**, sacred to Lord Hanuman; hence renamed **Hanumangarh**.

---

### 3.6 Lohagarh Fort (लोहागढ़ दुर्ग, Bharatpur) — The Invincible Mud Fortress
- **Classification**: A supreme synthesis of **Parikha Durg** (encircled by a deep moat) and **Jal-Mud Durg**.
- **Builder**: Constructed in **1733 CE** by **Maharaja Suraj Mal** (the "Plato of the Jat Tribe").
- **The Double Mud Ramparts**:
  - The outer fortifications consist of colossal thick walls of **packed clay and mud** encasing inner stone masonry.
  - When British siege artillery bombarded the fort, exploding iron cannonballs were harmlessly absorbed into the soft mud ramparts without causing the stone to shatter!
- **Sujan Ganga Moat (सुजान गंगा नहर)**:
  - Encircled by a deep, wide water canal (*Parikha*) fed by the waters of the **Ruparel (रूपा rail)** and **Banganga (बाणगंगा)** rivers via the Moti Jheel reservoir.
- **The Ashtadhatu Gates (अष्टधातु के किवाड़)**:
  - Historic eight-metal gates brought by **Maharaja Jawahar Singh** from Delhi's Red Fort in 1765 CE (originally looted by Alauddin Khalji from **Chittorgarh Fort in 1303**).
- **Defeat of Lord Lake (1805 CE)**: British Commander-in-Chief **Lord Lake** besieged Lohagarh Fort five consecutive times with massive siege trains, losing over 3,000 British soldiers before lifting the siege in defeat.

---

### 3.7 Siwana Fort & Jalore Fort

#### Siwana Fort (सिवाना दुर्ग, Balotra)
- **Topography**: Situated on the **Haldeshwar Hill (हल्देश्वर पहाड़ी)** in the Chhappan mountain range.
- **Builder**: Built in the 10th century (c. 954 CE) by **Veer Narayan Panwar** (son of Raja Bhoja).
- **Historical Nicknames**: *Kumtana Durg* (due to dense *Kumhat* thorny bushes); the **Sanctuary of Marwar Kings** (*मारवाड़ के राजाओं की शरणस्थली* — where Rao Maldeo retreated after Giri-Sumel and Rao Chandrasen based his guerrilla war).
- **Two Sākas of Siwana**:
  1. **First Sāka (1308 CE)**: Invader: Alauddin Khalji; Sovereign: **Sataldeo and Som**; traitor **Bhavla Pawar** poisoned the Bhandelav pond with cow-blood; fort captured and renamed **Khairabad (खैराबाद)**.
  2. **Second Sāka (1582 CE)**: Invader: Emperor Akbar; Sovereign: **Veer Kallaji Rathore** (nephew of Chandrasen) fought against Mota Raja Udai Singh.

#### Jalore Fort (जालोर दुर्ग) — Songadh
- **Topography**: Built upon the **Swarnagiri (कनकाचल / स्वर्णगिरि)** hill overlooking the **Sukri river**.
- **Builder**: Founded by Gurjara-Pratihara King **Nagabhata I** in the 8th century; golden age under the **Songara Chauhans**.
- **Hasan Nizami's Verdict**: In *Taj-ul-Ma'asir*, chronicler Hasan Nizami wrote:
  > *"Jalore is an unconquerable fortress whose monumental gates were never forced open by any invader on Earth!"*
- **The Sāka of Jalore (1311–1312 CE)**:
  - Invader: Alauddin Khalji; Sovereign: **Rao Kanhadadeva** and son **Viramdeo**.
  - Traitor **Bika Dahiya** revealed the secret unfortified mud breach to the Khalji army.
  - The famous Rajasthani proverb originated from this siege:
    > *"राई का भाव रात ही बीका!"*  
    *(The price of mustard seed expired overnight!)*
  - Kanhadadeva and Viramdeo fell in Kesariya; Queen Jetalde led Jauhar. Alauddin built the **Topkhana Mosque (तोपखाना मस्जिद)** inside the fort.

---85:T24ad,### 6.1 Section A: 2-Mark High-Density Formulations (15–20 Words)

#### Q1: Name the six hill forts of Rajasthan inscribed as UNESCO World Heritage sites in 2013.
**Answer**: Inscribed in June 2013: **Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Gagron, Jaisalmer, Ranthambore, and Amber** (*"चीकू गाजर आम"*).

#### Q2: What is the architectural significance of the Great Wall of Kumbhalgarh?
**Answer**: Spans **36 km** with a width of 15–20 ft (accommodating 4 horsemen abreast); world's second-longest continuous defensive wall after China's Great Wall.

#### Q3: Why is Gagron Fort designated as a supreme "Jal Durg"?
**Answer**: Surrounded by water on three sides at the confluence of the **Ahu and Kali Sindh** rivers, constructed without foundational trenches directly upon a rock cliff.

#### Q4: What was Abul Fazl’s verdict on Ranthambore Fort?
**Answer**: In *Akbarnama*, he remarked: *"All other forts are naked, but this fort is clad in mail armor!"* (*बख्तरबंद*), owing to its concealment within seven hills.

#### Q5: Define the construction uniqueness of Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Kila).
**Answer**: Erected on Trikuta Hill using golden-yellow jurassic sandstone **without mortar or lime**, relying exclusively on interlocking dry stone masonry.

#### Q6: Why is Junagarh Fort called "Zameen ka Zeewar"?
**Answer**: Built between 1589 and 1594 by Maharaja Rai Singh on level plains (*Bhu-Durg*) rather than a jagged mountain crag, radiating jewel-like architectural elegance.

#### Q7: What are the historical origins of the Ashtadhatu Gates of Lohagarh Fort?
**Answer**: Stolen by Alauddin Khalji from **Chittorgarh** to Delhi (1303); triumphantly brought by **Maharaja Jawahar Singh** from Delhi's Red Fort to Lohagarh in 1765.

---

### 6.2 Section B: 5-Mark Analytical Blueprints (50 Words)

#### Q8: Differentiate between Vijay Stambha and Jain Kirti Stambha in Chittorgarh Fort.
**Answer**:
Both are monumental towers in Chittorgarh displaying divergent purposes:
- **Vijay Stambha (1440–1448)**: 9 storeys (122 ft), commissioned by Maharana Kumbha to celebrate the victory at Sarangpur; dedicated to Lord Vishnu; designed by Jaita; inscribed by Atri-Mahesh; insignia of Rajasthan Police.
- **Jain Kirti Stambha (12th Century)**: 7 storeys (75 ft), built by Digambara Jain merchant Jija Bhagerwala; dedicated to 1st Tirthankara Lord Adinatha; decorated with Solanki-Jain Tirthankara relief carvings.

#### Q9: Analyze the strategic defense anatomy of Lohagarh Fort (Bharatpur).
**Answer**:
Built in 1733 by Maharaja Suraj Mal as an unbreachable Parikha-Mud citadel:
- **Double Mud Ramparts**: Thick outer walls of packed earth and clay absorbed heavy explosive British cannonballs without fracturing.
- **Sujan Ganga Moat**: Encircled by a deep water trench fed by the Ruparel and Banganga rivers, halting enemy mining.
- **Military Prowess**: Successfully repulsed five massive British artillery assaults under Commander-in-Chief Lord Lake in 1805.

#### Q10: Detail the architectural and strategic features of Katargarh within Kumbhalgarh Fort.
**Answer**:
Katargarh is the inner sovereign citadel crowning the highest peak of Kumbhalgarh:
- **"Eye of Mewar"**: Served as Maharana Kumbha’s personal palace and surveillance watchtower over Marwar-Mewar frontier borders.
- **Dizzying Height**: Abul Fazl noted that looking up from below causes the viewer's turban to fall off.
- **Historic Landmark**: Encloses the Badal Mahal, the sacred birthplace of **Maharana Pratap** (9 May 1540).

---

### 6.3 Section C: 10-Mark Multi-Dimensional Frameworks (100 Words)

#### Q11: "The fort architecture of Rajasthan reflects a masterly synthesis of geomorphic topography, defensive military strategy, and indigenous aesthetics." Elucidate with reference to the UNESCO Hill Forts.
**Answer**:
The six UNESCO Hill Forts of Rajasthan illustrate how medieval builders adapted regional topography into impregnable sovereign citadels:

│ 3. Material Ingenuity     │ • **Jaisalmer**: Built with yellow sandstone without lime/mortar, │
│                           │   using interlocking joints to resist arid thermal expansion.     │
│                           │ • **Amber**: Merged Rajput brackets with Mughal domes, Ganesh Pol │

├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│                           │   (Gaumukh, Padmala, Maota), guaranteeing years of siege survival.│
└───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
**Conclusion**: Rather than leveling the terrain, Rajasthani architects amplified nature’s rugged contours, producing monuments that harmonized martial invincibility with sublime aesthetic grandeur.

---

#### Q12: Trace the classification of forts as outlined in Shukraniti, and map them to historical examples in Rajasthan with their military significance.
**Answer**:
Shukraniti delineates a sophisticated **ninefold taxonomy (नवदुर्ग)** of fortresses, extensively mirrored across Rajasthan's defensive landscape:

1. **Giri Durg (Hill Fort — Declared Supreme)**:
   - *Example*: **Chittorgarh**, **Kumbhalgarh**, **Taragarh (Ajmer)**.
   - *Significance*: High elevation provided vast artillery command, long-range reconnaissance, and natural vertical cliffs that prevented battering-ram assaults.

2. **Jal / Audaka Durg (Water Fort)**:
   - *Example*: **Gagron Fort** (Ahu-Kali Sindh), **Bhainsrorgarh Fort** (Chambal-Bamni).
   - *Significance*: Water bodies on multiple flanks prevented enemy cavalry encirclement and sapping.

3. **Dhanvan Durg (Desert Fort)**:
   - *Example*: **Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Kila)**, **Bhatner Fort (Hanumangarh)**.
   - *Significance*: Remote sand dunes created logistical nightmares of water and fodder scarcity for invading imperial armies.

4. **Vana & Eerana Durg (Forest & Thorny Rock Fort)**:
   - *Example*: **Ranthambore Fort**, **Siwana Fort** (*Kumtana*).
   - *Significance*: Hidden by dense thorn forests and gorges, denying enemy artillery direct line-of-sight.

5. **Parikha Durg (Moat-Encircled Fort)**:
   - *Example*: **Lohagarh Fort (Bharatpur)**.
   - *Significance*: Deep water trenches (Sujan Ganga) neutralized subterranean mining, scaling ladders, and explosive petards.

6. **Paridha Durg (Massive Walled Fort)**:
   - *Example*: **Kumbhalgarh Fort** (36 km perimeter wall).
   - *Significance*: Provided impenetrable stone barriers shielding inner civilian populations, temples, and grain reserves.

They synthesized Rajput traditional spatial planning (*Zanana* and *Mardana* segregation, *Jharokhas*, *Chhatris*, and *Bari*) with Mughal elements (fluted arches, cusped vaults, mirrored mosaics, and water cascades).

### 1.1 City Palace, Udaipur (उदयपुर का राजमहल)
- **Foundational Epoch**: Commenced in **1559 CE by Maharana Udai Singh II** along the eastern embankment of Lake Pichola; successively expanded over 400 years by 22 successive Maharanas without breaking architectural harmony.
- **James Fergusson's Verdict**: The British architectural historian James Fergusson famously characterized it as the **"Windsor of Rajasthan"** (*राजस्थान का विंडसर महल*) due to its colossal scale, dramatic lakeside cliff setting, and granite-marble masonry.
- **Architectural Anatomy & Key Pavilions**:
  1. **Badi Mahal (Garden Palace)**: Constructed on a natural 90-foot hillock enclosed within the upper palace, featuring 104 carved marble pillars, cisterns, and lush fruit trees.
  2. **Chandra Mahal & Dilkhush Mahal**: Intricately adorned with Belgian glass mosaics, mirrored walls, and traditional Mewari miniature murals.
  3. **Moti Mahal & Sheesh Mahal**: Built by Maharana Karan Singh (1620–1628), showcasing early Mughal architectural integration.
  4. **Toran Pol & Badi Pol**: Grand entrance portals; outside Badi Pol sits the historic *Hathi Agad* (arena for elephant duels).
  5. **Mor Chowk (Peacock Courtyard)**: Executed during Maharana Sajjan Singh’s reign; adorned with three world-renowned relief peacocks crafted from over 5,000 brilliant green, blue, and gold glass tesserae representing summer, monsoon, and winter.

### 1.2 City Palace & Hawa Mahal, Jaipur

#### City Palace Complex (Chandra Mahal)
- **Genesis & Layout**: Commissioned in **1727 CE by Sawai Jai Singh II** and designed by chief architect **Vidyadhar Bhattacharya** according to Vastu Purusha Mandala principles. Occupies one-seventh of the walled city of Jaipur.
- **Chandra Mahal (Moon Palace)**: The monumental seven-storeyed sanctum sanctorum of the Kachhwaha dynasty:
  - *Ground Floor*: Pitam Niwas / Sukh Niwas.
  - *Second Floor*: Rang Mandir.
  - *Third Floor*: Shobha Niwas (Mica and mirror decoration).
  - *Fourth Floor*: Chhavi Niwas (Blue and white monochrome Chinese porcelain patterns).
  - *Fifth Floor*: Shri Niwas.
  - *Sixth Floor*: Mukut Mandir (Crowned apex displaying the royal *Pachranga* flag).
- **Mubarak Mahal**: Built in the late 19th century by **Sawai Madho Singh II** as a royal reception pavilion (*Welcome Palace*); designed by British architect **Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob** in an ornate Indo-Saracenic synthesis combining Mughal, Rajput, and European classical styles.
- **Pritam Niwas Chowk (Courtyard of the Beloved)**: Inner courtyard renowned for its four vibrantly painted gateway arches dedicated to the four seasons and Hindu deities:
  1. *Peacock Gate* (North-East, dedicated to Lord Vishnu / Autumn).
  2. *Lotus Gate* (South-West, dedicated to Shiva-Parvati / Summer).
  3. *Green / Waves Gate* (North-West, dedicated to Lord Ganesha / Monsoon).
  4. *Rose Gate* (South-East, dedicated to Devi / Winter).
- **The Gangajalis (Guinness World Record)**: Two colossal sterling silver vessels displayed in the *Diwan-i-Khas*, commissioned by Sawai Madho Singh II in 1901 to carry 4,000 liters of holy Ganges water for his voyage to London for King Edward VII's coronation. They are certified as the largest single-piece silver vessels in the world (each weighing 340 kg).

#### Hawa Mahal (हवामहल) — "Palace of the Breeze"
- **Date & Patron**: Erected in **1799 CE by Sawai Pratap Singh**; envisioned as an extension of the City Palace *Zanana*.
- **Master Architect**: **Ustad Lal Chand Ustad** (उस्ताद लाल चंद).
- **Iconography**: Shaped in the silhouette of the divine crown (*Mukut*) of **Lord Krishna**, whom Sawai Pratap Singh devoutly worshipped under his pen name *Brijnidhi*.
- **Architectural Mechanics**:
  - Soars **five storeys high (87 feet)** without any traditional deep foundation pit; constructed entirely on a slender 8-inch base wall using red and pink sandstone.
  - Features **953 intricately carved latticed stone windows (*Jharokhas*)** and tiny casements (*Jalis*).
  - Utilizes the **Venturi effect**: air passing through narrow perforations accelerates and undergoes adiabatic cooling, ensuring a continuous chilled breeze during peak summer.
  - Built explicitly so royal secluded ladies (*Pardanashin Zanana*) could discreetly observe bustling street pageants and religious processions (*Teej*, *Gangaur*) along Badi Chaupar without being viewed by the public.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    THE FIVE TIERS / STOREYS OF HAWA MAHAL (JAIPUR)                     │
├───────┬──────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Tier  │ Name of Floor (Storey)       │ Architectural Identity & Function               │
├───────┼──────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 5th   │ **Hawa Mandir**              │ Topmost windswept pavilion; gave palace its name│
│ 4th   │ **Prakash Mandir**           │ Open terrace flooded with natural solar light   │
│ 3rd   │ **Vichitra Mandir**          │ Intimate prayer room where Pratap Singh sang    │
│ 2nd   │ **Ratan Mandir**             │ Decorated with dazzling colored glass work      │
│ 1st   │ **Sharad Mandir** (Pratap)   │ Ground autumn pavilion; autumn festivities      │
└───────┴──────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
> **Mnemonic for Hawa Mahal Storeys**: *"शरद रतन विचित्र प्रकाश हवा"* (Sharad $\rightarrow$ Ratan $\rightarrow$ Vichitra $\rightarrow$ Prakash $\rightarrow$ Hawa).

---87:T2bfd,Havelis (*हवेलियाँ*) were private residential mansions built by wealthy prime ministers, royal treasurers (*Diwans*), feudal thakurs, and prominent Marwari merchant families (*Seth-Sahukars*). They reached their artistic zenith during the 18th, 19th, and early 20th centuries, functioning as secure urban fortresses, business offices (*Gaddis*), and social showpieces.

### 2.1 The Golden Havelis of Jaisalmer

#### 1. Patwon ki Haveli (पटवों की हवेली) — The Crown Jewel
- **Founder & Date**: Commissioned by **Guman Chand Patwa** (a wealthy merchant of brocade, jewelry, and opium) in **1805 CE**.
- **Structural Blueprint**: A colossal cluster of **five separate storeys/mansions** built over a span of 50 years for his five sons.
- **Architectural Excellence**:
  - The first and grandest haveli constructed in Jaisalmer.
  - Carved entirely from golden-yellow Jurassic limestone; famous for over **60 unique open balconies (*Jharokhas*)**, perforated floral lattices, and slender stone balustrades carved so thinly that stone resembles spun lace.

#### 2. Salim Singh ki Haveli (सालिम सिंह की हवेली)
- **Founder**: Commissioned in **1815 CE by Salim Singh Mohta**, the eccentric and ruthless prime minister (*Diwan*) of Jaisalmer State.
- **Unique Silhouette**:
  - Built with a narrow stone base that fans outward dramatically on the fifth and sixth storeys, resembling the prow of a sailing ship — hence titled **Jahaz Mahal** (*जहाज महल*).
  - The upper cantilevered floor features 38 intricately sculpted balconies crowned with dancing peacock brackets (*Moti Mahal*). Originally possessed two wooden/glass top storeys, which were dismantled by order of the Maharawal due to royal jealousy.

#### 3. Nathmal ki Haveli (नथमल की हवेली)
- **Patron**: Built in **1885 CE** as the official residence for Diwan Mohata Nathmal.
- **Twin Master Sculptors**: Carved simultaneously by two Muslim architect brothers, **Hathi (हाथी)** and **Lalu (लालू)**. One brother carved the right half and the other carved the left half independently. Though symmetrically unified from a distance, minute examination reveals that no two architectural panels or jali screens are identical.
- **Unique Embellishments**: Two life-sized stone elephants (*Hathi*) flank the main arched entry gate; features early carvings of steam engines, bicycles, and wristwatches based on the brothers' descriptions of modern inventions they had never seen firsthand.

---

### 2.2 The Painted Havelis of Shekhawati — "Open-Air Art Gallery"
The arid triangle of Shekhawati (spanning Sikar, Jhunjhunu, and Churu districts) possesses the world's highest concentration of painted frescoed mansions, earning it global acclaim as the **"Open-Air Art Gallery of Rajasthan"**.

#### The Fresco Techniques: Arayash / Ala-Gila / Mora-Kashi
To withstand scorching summer heat and desert dust storms, Shekhawati artists (*Chiteras*) perfected traditional mural plastering methods:
1. **Fresco Buono (Ala-Gila / Arayash / गीला पलस्तर)**:
   - Pigments ground from natural minerals (lapis lazuli for blue, cinnabar for red, yellow ochre, copper sulfate for green, and soot for black) were applied directly onto **fresh, wet lime plaster**.
   - As the slaked lime plaster (*Chuna*) dried, calcium hydroxide reacted with atmospheric carbon dioxide to form insoluble calcium carbonate, binding the pigments permanently into the wall fabric itself.
   - The surface was buffed vigorously with smooth agate stones (*Ghutai*) until it achieved a mirror-like marble sheen.
2. **Fresco Secco**: Pigments applied onto dried lime wash using organic binders (glue or gum), used for faster, less durable exterior embellishments.

#### The Thematic Evolution of Shekhawati Murals
- **Phase 1 (18th – Mid 19th Century)**: Strictly religious, mythological, and local folk themes: Krishna Leela, Raslila, Ramayana episodes, Dhola-Maru, Pabuji, and equestrian hunts.
- **Phase 2 (Late 19th – Early 20th Century)**: British colonial impact: Portraits of Queen Victoria, British soldiers with muskets, steam locomotives, phonographs, motorcars, hot air balloons, and telephones painted alongside traditional deities.

### 2.3 Other Notable Havelis of Rajasthan
- **Rampuria Havelis, Bikaner**: Built by merchant Baldeo Das Rampuria using fine red **Dulmera sandstone**; celebrated for their fusion of traditional Jharokhas with Victorian European floral relief brackets.
- **Bade Devtaji ki Haveli & Jhala Ji ki Haveli, Kota**: Acclaimed for exceptional wall paintings executed in the classical **Kota School of Painting** (hunting expeditions, royal durbars).
- **Pungaliya Haveli & Bade Miyan ki Haveli, Jodhpur**: Ornate red sandstone lattice screens with characteristic Marwari arches.
- **Bagore ki Haveli, Udaipur**: Perched at Gangaur Ghat on Lake Pichola; built by Mewar Prime Minister **Amarchand Barwa**; houses the world's largest turban and a preserved royal puppet theater.

---88:T225e,In the arid and semi-arid terrain of Rajasthan, water architecture transcended utilitarian storage to become sacred community monuments. Stepwells (*Baori* / *Bawdi* / *Vapi*) combined deep subterranean wells with descending stepped corridors, pillared pavilions, and stone idols of water and fertility deities.

### 3.1 Chand Baori, Abhaneri (चाँद बावड़ी, आभानेरी)
- **Location**: Abhaneri village, Bandikui, **Dausa district**.
- **Epoch & Builder**: Constructed in the **8th–9th century CE** by **Raja Chand (Nikumbha Rajput ruler)** of ancient *Abha-Nagari* (City of Brightness).
- **Architectural Anatomy**:
  - The **deepest and most geometrically complex stepwell in the world**: drops over **100 feet (13 storeys)** into the earth.
  - Comprises precisely **3,500 crisscrossing steps** arranged in perfectly symmetrical double-diamond flight patterns.
  - The steps are engineered with optical illusion precision: an individual ascending the steps cannot traverse the exact same staircase configuration taken while descending.
  - The northern face contains multi-tiered arched pavilions (*Chhatris*) housing carved statues of Mahishasuramardini and Lord Ganesha, serving as the royal rest chambers.
  - Overlooks the adjoining 8th-century **Harshat Mata Temple** (a masterpiece of Gurjara-Pratihara temple art).

---

### 3.2 Raniji ki Baori, Bundi (रानीजी की बावड़ी) — "The Queen of Stepwells"
- **Location**: Bundi, officially celebrated as the **"City of Stepwells"** (*बावड़ियों का शहर*).
- **Founding Monarch**: Built in **1699 CE by Rani Nathavati** (consort of Rao Raja Aniruddha Singh and mother of Maharao Budh Singh).
- **Dimensions & Artistic Grandeur**:
  - Drops **150 feet** deep; entered through a magnificent freestanding stone ceremonial archway (*Torana Dwar*).
  - Flanked by four soaring sculpted pillars terminating in bracketed capitals with life-sized sculpted elephants (*Gaj-Lakshmi*).
  - Contains intricate niche shrines displaying the ten incarnations (*Dashavatara*) of Lord Vishnu along its subterranean stairs.
  - Acknowledged as the most ornate and architecturally flawless stepwell in south-eastern Rajasthan.

---89:T2ba4,Chhatris (*छतरियाँ*) are elevated, domed commemorative cenotaphs erected over the cremation sites of kings, queens, feudal nobility, war heroes, and ascetic saints. Rooted in ancient Hindu funerary stambhas, they developed under Rajput patronage into sublime open-pillared pavilions adorned with carved domes, decorative finials (*Amalaka & Kalasha*), and central equestrian or Shiva lingam steles.

### 4.1 Master Individual Chhatris of Rajasthan

#### 1. 84-Pillared Chhatri, Bundi (चौरासी खंभों की छतरी)
- **Patron & Date**: Commissioned in **1683 CE by Rao Raja Aniruddha Singh** in memory of his beloved foster brother **Dhaabhai Deva (धाभाई देवा)**.
- **Structural Blueprint**:
  - Two-storeyed pavilion supported by **precisely 84 carved stone pillars**.
  - Lower floor contains a central sacred **Shiva Lingam** surrounded by carvings of animals, dancers, and musicians.
  - The upper floor features 16 central pillars supporting a grand fluted dome flanked by four corner chhatris.

#### 2. Moosi Maharani ki Chhatri, Alwar (मूसी महारानी की छतरी)
- **Patron & Date**: Constructed in **1815 CE by Maharaja Vinay Singh** in memory of his predecessor **Maharaja Bakhtawar Singh** and his consort **Moosi Maharani**, who performed Sati.
- **Architectural Synthesis**:
  - Supported by **80 carved pillars**.
  - **Bichromatic Masonry**: The lower storey is carved from rugged red sandstone, while the upper storey is crafted from pure white Makrana marble with Bengal-style vaulted cornices (*Bangaldar Chhatri*).
  - Ceiling contains murals depicting the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

#### 3. Jaswant Thada, Jodhpur (जसवंत थड़ा) — "The Taj Mahal of Marwar"
- **Patron & Date**: Erected in **1899 CE by Maharaja Sardar Singh** to commemorate his father, **Maharaja Jaswant Singh II**.
- **Architectural Marvel**:
  - Carved entirely from paper-thin, polished sheets of **Makrana white marble**.
  - The marble slabs are carved so thinly that sunlight penetrates the solid walls, casting a translucent golden-white inner luminescence.
  - Encloses memorial portraits of Jodhpur rulers, intricately landscaped gardens, and a sacred cremation lake.

---8a:T497c,Temple architecture in Rajasthan spans over fifteen centuries, serving as the crucible for the evolution of the North Indian **Nagara Style**, culminating in the indigenous **Maha-Maru (महा-मारू)** and **Maru-Gurjara (मारू-गुर्जर / सोलंकी)** idioms.

---

### 5.1 The Earliest Inscribed Temple: Sheetleshwar Mahadev, Jhalrapatan (689 CE)
- Located at **Jhalrapatan (Jhalawar)** on the banks of the Chandrabhaga river.
- Bearing an epigraph of **689 CE (V.S. 746)** from the reign of king Durgagana, it is officially recognized as the **oldest dated temple in Rajasthan** (*राजस्थान का प्रथम तिथि-अंकित मंदिर*). Built by royal architect Voppa.

---

### 5.2 The Gurjara-Pratihara / Maha-Maru Style (8th–11th Century CE)

#### 1. Osian Temple Complex, Jodhpur Rural (ओसियां)
- Celebrated as the **"Khajuraho / Bhuvaneshwar of Rajasthan"**; served as the prime socio-religious capital of the Gurjara-Pratiharas.
- Contains 16 Hindu and Jain temples dating between the 8th and 11th centuries:
  - **Mahavira Temple**: Erected during the reign of **Pratihara king Vatsaraja (778–794 CE)**; universally acknowledged as the **oldest surviving Jain temple in western India**.
  - **Sachiya Mata Temple**: Consecrated to Mahishasuramardini; revered as the family deity (*Kuldevi*) of the **Oswal Jain community**.
  - **Surya Temples**: Three distinct sun temples boasting elaborately carved sanctum doorframes (*Dwar-Sakhas*) depicting Navagrahas and flying Gandharvas.

#### 2. Kiradu Temple Complex, Barmer (किराडू के मंदिर)
- Located at the foot of Hathma village hills in Barmer; ancient epigraphic name: **Kiratkoot (किराटकूट)**.
- Famous as the **"Khajuraho of Rajasthan"** (*राजस्थान का खजुराहो*) due to its masterfully sculpted human figures, sensuous erotic reliefs, and celestial musicians (*Apsaras*).
- Comprises five temples (four dedicated to Shiva and one to Vishnu), with the **Someshwara Temple (सोमेश्वर मंदिर)** being the largest and most architecturally complete. Built in the late Gurjara-Pratihara / early Solanki transitional style (11th–12th century).

#### 3. Other Maha-Maru Shrines
- **Harshat Mata Temple, Abhaneri (Dausa)**: 8th-century sanctuary dedicated to the Goddess of Joy; exquisite bas-reliefs of dance, music, and divine love.
- **Harshnath Temple, Sikar**: Built in **973 CE by Chauhan ruler Vigraharaja II**; designed by ascetic Allata; dedicated to Lord Shiva atop Harsh Hill.
- **Baroli Temple Complex, Rawatbhata (Chittorgarh)**: 9th-century Panchayatana temples dedicated to Ghateshwar Mahadev on the Chambal river; acclaimed by James Tod for flawless proportions.

---

### 5.3 The Maru-Gurjara Masterpieces: Dilwara & Ranakpur

#### 1. Dilwara Jain Temples, Mount Abu (देलवाड़ा के जैन मंदिर)
Perched on the granite heights of Mount Abu (Sirohi), the five marble Dilwara temples represent the absolute apex of medieval stone filigree in world history. Colonel James Tod proclaimed: *"Beyond the Taj Mahal, there is no monument in India that approaches the finish and beauty of the Dilwara temples."*

#### 2. Ranakpur Jain Temple, Pali (रणकपुर का चौमुखा जैन मंदिर)
- **Geographic Setting**: Situated in the dense Aravali gorge of Sadri, Desuri tehsil, **Pali district**, along the banks of the **Maghai river**.
- **Historical Era**: Commenced in **1439 CE** during the glorious reign of **Maharana Kumbha of Mewar**.
- **The Pious Merchant**: Commissioned and funded by the wealthy Jain Porwal merchant **Dharanashah (धरणशाह / धरणा शाह)** after receiving a divine vision of a celestial aerial vehicle (*Nalini-Gulma Vimana*). Maharana Kumbha gifted the surrounding land and village.
- **The Master Architect**: **Depaka (देपाका / दीपा)**, whose genius transformed white Makrana marble into a sprawling three-dimensional sacred labyrinth.
- **Dedication**: Dedicated to the 1st Jain Tirthankara, **Bhagwan Adinatha (Rishabhadeva)**.
- **The Chaumukha Configuration**: Features a 6-foot four-faced white marble idol of Adinatha facing all four cardinal directions, allowing worshippers to glimpse the Tirthankara from any quadrant of the sanctum.
- **Architectural Mechanics & The "Forest of Pillars"**:
  - Contains precisely **1,444 intricately sculpted marble pillars** (*स्तंभों का वन*).
  - **Sovereign Engineering Feat**: Despite 1,444 pillars, **no single pillar obstructs the direct line of sight** between a devotee standing anywhere in the peripheral colonnades and the central idol.
  - **Unique Carvings**: Every single pillar exhibits a distinct decorative motif; no two pillars are carved identically.
  - Features 84 secondary shrines (*Devakulikas*), 29 halls (*Mandapas*), and 4 grand entrance halls.
- **Classic Epigraphic Epithets**:
  - *Dharani-Vihara* (धरण विहार — named after Dharanashah).
  - *Trailokya Dipaka* (त्रैलोक्य दीपक — "Illuminator of the Three Realms").
  - *Khabhon ka Ajaibghar* (Museum of Pillars).

---

---8b:T15d9,1. **The "Windsor of Rajasthan" Attribution**: The City Palace of **Udaipur** was called the "Windsor of Rajasthan" by British architectural historian **James Fergusson**, NOT James Tod.
2. **Hawa Mahal Architect vs Founder**: Founded by **Sawai Pratap Singh (1799)**; designed by architect **Ustad Lal Chand Ustad**. It has **no regular foundation** and sits directly on a narrow stone base.
3. **The Five Storeys of Hawa Mahal Sequence**: Bottom to top: (1) Sharad Mandir, (2) Ratan Mandir, (3) Vichitra Mandir, (4) Prakash Mandir, (5) Hawa Mandir. If RPSC asks which floor gives the monument its name, it is the **topmost 5th floor (Hawa Mandir)**.
4. **Sterling Silver Gangajalis Location**: The world's largest silver vessels are housed in the **Diwan-i-Khas of City Palace, Jaipur**, commissioned by **Sawai Madho Singh II** for his 1901 voyage to England.
5. **Umaid Bhawan Palace Builder & Alternate Name**: Built by **Maharaja Umaid Singh** between 1929 and 1943 as a famine relief project (*Akal Rahat Karya*); called **Chittar Palace** because it is built from local golden *Chittar* sandstone; designed by British architect **Henry Vaughan Lanchester**.
6. **The First vs Grandest Haveli in Jaisalmer**: **Patwon ki Haveli** was the first haveli built in Jaisalmer (1805 CE, Guman Chand Patwa, 5 storeys for 5 sons). **Salim Singh ki Haveli** is shaped like a ship (*Jahaz Mahal*).
7. **The Non-Identical Symmetry of Nathmal ki Haveli**: Carved by two brothers, **Hathi and Lalu**, who carved left and right halves simultaneously without looking at each other's designs, resulting in intentional, microscopic asymmetries.
8. **The Ala-Gila / Arayash Plaster Formula**: *Ala-Gila* is the technique of applying pigments onto **wet lime plaster** (*Fresco Buono*), buffed with agate stone (*Ghutai*) to create a marble shine. It originated in Jaipur and spread across Shekhawati.
9. **Haveli with 1,111 Windows and Doors**: **Surana Haveli** in **Churu**, famously known as the *"Hawa Mahal of Churu"*.
10. **The Golden City of Shekhawati**: **Nawalgarh** is titled the "Golden City of Shekhawati" due to its dense cluster of painted havelis (Poddar, Aath Haveli, Chokhani).
11. **Deepest Stepwell in the World**: **Chand Baori** in **Abhaneri (Dausa)**, 13 storeys, 100 feet deep, with **3,500 symmetrical steps** built by Nikumbha king Raja Chand (8th–9th century).
12. **The "City of Stepwells"**: **Bundi** is officially titled *"बावड़ियों का शहर"* (City of Stepwells). Its most famous stepwell is **Raniji ki Baori**, built in 1699 by Rani Nathavati.
13. **Subterranean Multi-Storey Stepwells**: **Neemrana Baori** in Kotputli-Behror has **9 storeys**; **Chand Baori** has **13 storeys**.
14. **The Exception to Gaitore Royal Cremations**: All Kachhwaha rulers of Jaipur from Sawai Jai Singh II onwards are cremated at **Gaitore**, EXCEPT **Sawai Ishwari Singh**, whose chhatri is located inside the City Palace compound near **Talkatora** (due to his suicide over Maratha debt).
15. **The "Taj Mahal of Marwar"**: **Jaswant Thada** in **Jodhpur**, built in 1899 by **Maharaja Sardar Singh** for his father Maharaja Jaswant Singh II, using translucent white Makrana marble.
16. **84-Pillared vs 80-Pillared Chhatri**:
    - **84-Pillared Chhatri**: Located in **Bundi**, built in 1683 by Rao Raja Aniruddha Singh for foster brother **Dhaabhai Deva**.
    - **80-Pillared Chhatri**: Located in **Alwar**, built in 1815 by Maharaja Vinay Singh for **Bakhtawar Singh & Moosi Maharani**.
17. **32-Pillared Chhatri Dual Confusion**:
    - **Ranthambore Fort**: Built by Hammiradeva for his father **Jaitrasimha's 32-year reign** (*Nyaya ki Chhatri*).
    - **Mandalgarh (Bhilwara)**: Built for Mughal commander **Jagannath Kachhwaha**.
18. **Oldest Inscribed Dated Temple in Rajasthan**: **Sheetleshwar Mahadev Temple** at **Jhalrapatan (Jhalawar)**, dated **689 CE (V.S. 746)** from King Durgagana's reign.
19. **Oldest Surviving Jain Temple in Western India**: **Mahavira Temple at Osian** (Jodhpur Rural), built during the reign of Pratihara king **Vatsaraja** (8th century CE).
20. **The "Khajuraho of Rajasthan"**: **Kiradu Temples** in **Barmer** (specifically the Someshwara temple). Do NOT confuse with:
    - *"Mini Khajuraho / Khajuraho of Hadoti"*: **Bhanddevara Temple** (Ramgarh, Baran).
    - *"Khajuraho of Mewar"*: **Ambika Mata Temple** (Jagat, Udaipur).
21. **Vimal Vasahi vs Luna Vasahi Architects & Patrons**:
    - **Vimal Vasahi (1031 CE)**: Patron = Vimal Shah; Architect = **Kirti Dhara**; Dedicated to Adinatha.
    - **Luna Vasahi (1230 CE)**: Patron = Vastupala & Tejapala; Architect = **Shobhana Deva**; Dedicated to Neminatha; Contains *Derani-Jethani Gokhla*.
22. **The 1,444 Pillars of Ranakpur**: Ranakpur Jain Temple has **1,444 pillars**, built in **1439 CE** during Maharana Kumbha's reign by merchant **Dharanashah** and architect **Depaka**. It is dedicated to **Adinatha (Rishabhadeva)**.
23. **"Sapno se bana Mandir" (Temple Built of Dreams)**: The **Jagdish Temple** in Udaipur, built in **1651 CE by Maharana Jagat Singh I** (Architect: Barna), dedicated to Lord Vishnu in the Panchayatana style.
24. **Eklingji Temple Dedication & Sect**: Dedicated to Lord Shiva's **Lakulisha sect** (Pashupata); four-faced black marble Shivalinga founded by Bappa Rawal in 734 CE.
25. **The Bearded Hanuman Shrine**: **Salasar Balaji** in **Churu district** contains the only idol in Rajasthan representing Lord Hanuman with a **beard and mustache** (*दाढ़ी-मूँछ वाले हनुमान जी*).

---8c:T2c6c,### 7.1 2-Markers (15–20 Words)

#### Q1: What is the architectural significance of Raniji ki Baori in Bundi?
**Answer**:
Built in 1699 CE by Rani Nathavati, this 150-foot deep stepwell features a grand *Torana Dwar*, high-relief *Gaj-Lakshmi* pillar brackets, and sculpted *Dashavatara* niches, representing the apex of Hadoti water architecture.

---

#### Q2: Name the master architect and the patron of Ranakpur Jain Temple.
**Answer**:
Commissioned and funded in 1439 CE by the Jain Porwal merchant **Dharanashah** under the royal patronage of **Maharana Kumbha**; engineered by master architect **Depaka**.

---

#### Q3: What is the "Ala-Gila" or "Arayash" technique?
**Answer**:
A traditional Rajasthani *Fresco Buono* plaster method where mineral pigments are applied directly onto wet slaked lime plaster and buffed with agate stone, binding colors permanently with a marble-like luster.

---

#### Q4: Why is Jaswant Thada termed the "Taj Mahal of Marwar"?
**Answer**:
Erected in Jodhpur (1899 CE) by Maharaja Sardar Singh for Jaswant Singh II, it is constructed from paper-thin, polished Makrana white marble that glows translucently under sunlight.

---

#### Q5: State the key architectural feature of the Dilwara Luna Vasahi temple.
**Answer**:
Built in 1230 CE by Vastupala-Tejapala (architect Shobhana Deva) dedicated to Neminatha; renowned for its delicate marble pendant dome and the intricately carved *Derani-Jethani ka Gokhla*.

---

### 7.2 5-Markers (50 Words)

#### Q6: Analyze the functional and bioclimatic architecture of Hawa Mahal in Jaipur.
**Answer**:
Erected in 1799 CE by Sawai Pratap Singh and designed by Ustad Lal Chand, Hawa Mahal is a 5-storeyed, 87-foot monument without deep foundations, shaped like Lord Krishna’s crown.
1. **Bioclimatic Engineering**: Its 953 stone *Jharokhas* and latticed *Jalis* exploit the **Venturi effect**, cooling incoming desert wind through adiabatic pressure drops.
2. **Socio-Cultural Function**: Permitted royal *Pardanashin* women to observe city festivals and processions on Badi Chaupar without violating purdah seclusion.

---

#### Q7: Delineate the distinct architectural and decorative characteristics of Shekhawati havelis.
**Answer**:
Developed by Marwari merchants during the 18th to early 20th centuries across Sikar, Jhunjhunu, and Churu, Shekhawati havelis represent an "Open-Air Art Gallery":
1. **Spatial Plan**: Dual-courtyard layout separating outer commercial spaces (*Mardana*) from inner domestic spaces (*Zanana*).
2. **Fresco Buono**: Exterior and interior walls plastered using *Arayash/Ala-Gila* techniques with natural mineral pigments.
3. **Thematic Evolution**: Shifted from Krishna Leela and folk epics (Dhola-Maru) to colonial innovations (railway trains, motorcars, and airplanes).

---

#### Q8: Write a concise note on the Gurjara-Pratihara (Maha-Maru) temple style with two examples.
**Answer**:
Flourishing between the 8th and 11th centuries CE in Rajasthan, the **Maha-Maru style** is distinguished by elevated carved plinths (*Jagati*), clustered curvilinear *Shikharas*, ornate doorframes (*Dwar-Sakhas*) depicting river goddesses (Ganga-Yamuna), and rich pediments:
1. **Mahavira Temple, Osian (Jodhpur Rural)**: Consecrated under Pratihara king Vatsaraja (8th century); oldest surviving Jain shrine in western India.
2. **Kiradu Temples (Barmer)**: Someshwara Shiva temple, celebrated as the "Khajuraho of Rajasthan" for its exquisite sculptures.

---

### 7.3 10-Markers (100 Words)

#### Q9: "Water architecture in Rajasthan was not merely an engineering response to aridity, but a sacred synthesis of community life, aesthetics, and structural genius." Critically evaluate with reference to Baoris and Kunds.
**Answer**:
In arid Rajasthan, scarce rainfall compelled medieval society to treat water conservation as an act of divine piety (*Purta Dharma*), synthesizing hydraulic mechanics with public art:

**Conclusion**: Rajasthani stepwells transformed harsh hydrological necessity into monumental sacred spaces, establishing an enduring benchmark in sustainable vernacular architecture.

[Chapter 12 Complete ➔ Next: Chapter 13: Schools of Rajasthani Painting]8d:T205e,Rajasthani painting (*राजस्थानी चित्रकला*) represents one of the most vibrant, emotionally intense, and stylistically distinct traditions of visual art in South Asia. Derived from the ancient Western Indian miniature style (Apabhramsha and Jain manuscript painting), it blossomed into an independent indigenous aesthetic between the 15th and 19th centuries under the royal patronage of Rajput principalities.

```

          │                                       │                                       │

### 1.1 The Pioneer Scholars & Terminological Debate
1. **Dr. Anand Kentish Coomaraswamy (1916)**:
   - In his groundbreaking two-volume treatise **"Rajput Painting" (1916)**, Coomaraswamy became the first scholar to scientifically classify traditional Indian painting.
   - He drew a sharp aesthetic and philosophical distinction between **Mughal Painting** (secular, courtly, aristocratic, portraiture-driven, realistic) and **Rajput Painting** (sacred, devotional, folk-grounded, lyrical, romantic).
   - Under the umbrella of *Rajput Painting*, he grouped two major geographical branches: (a) **Rajasthani School** (Plains of Rajputana) and (b) **Pahari School** (Himalayan sub-states such as Kangra, Basohli, and Guler).
2. **O.C. Gangoly & Basil Gray**: Authored *Masterpieces of Rajput Painting*, supporting the dynastic and aristocratic nomenclature "Rajput School".
3. **Rai Krishnadas**: In his seminal work *Bharat ki Chitrakala*, he strongly argued that the term "Rajput Painting" was misleadingly communal/dynastic, since artists, subjects, and themes encompassed all social strata. He firmly established the universally accepted academic term **"Rajasthani Chitrasheili" (राजस्थानी चित्रशैली)** based on geographical and linguistic sovereignty.
4. **Other Canonical Historians**: W.G. Archer (*Indian Paintings in Rajasthan*), Dr. Moti Chandra, Dr. Shridhar Andhare, Karl Khandalavala, and Ramgopal Vijayvargiya.

---

### 1.2 The Four Regional Schools (School of Art / Chitra-School)
Based on geographic proximity, dynastic patronage, stylistic brushwork, facial profiles, and environmental color palettes, Rajasthani painting is classified into **Four Canonical Schools**, encompassing over a dozen distinct sub-styles (*Upashailiyan*):

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               THE FOUR REGIONAL SCHOOLS OF RAJASTHANI PAINTING                         │

│ Primary School             │ Geographic Scope            │ Sub-Styles (Upashailiyan)   │
├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ **1. Mewar School**        │ South & South-West Raj.     │ • Udaipur Sub-style         │
│ (The Mother Style)         │ (Mewar Plateau & Hills)     │ • Nathdwara Sub-style       │
│                            │                             │ • Chavand Sub-style         │
│                            │                             │ • Devgarh & Shahpura        │
├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ **2. Marwar School**       │ West & North-West Raj.      │ • Jodhpur Sub-style         │
│ (Desert & Sand Dunes)      │ (Thar Desert Principalities)│ • Bikaner Sub-style         │
│                            │                             │ • Kishangarh Sub-style      │
│                            │                             │ • Nagaur & Jaisalmer        │
├────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ **3. Dhundhar School**     │ North-East & Central Raj.   │ • Amer / Jaipur Sub-style   │

│                            │                             │ • Shekhawati Sub-style      │

│ **4. Hadoti School**       │ South-East Raj.             │ • Bundi Sub-style           │
│ (Hadoti Plateau / Chambal) │ (Hada Rajput territory)     │ • Kota Sub-style            │
│                            │                             │ • Jhalawar Sub-style        │
└────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘
```

---8e:T25ee,The Mewar School is universally revered as the **fountainhead / mother style** of all Rajasthani painting. Being the most geographically insulated from Delhi and fiercely resistant to Mughal subjugation, Mewar preserved the purest indigenous traits of Western Indian art.

```

### 2.1 Earliest Manuscript Inscriptions
1. **Shravaka Pratikramana Sutra Churni (श्रावक प्रतिक्रमण सूत्र चूर्णी)**:
   - **Date & Location**: Executed in **1260 CE (V.S. 1317)** at **Ahar (Mewar)**.
   - **Patron Monarch**: Guhil king **Rawal Tejasimha (रावल तेजसिंह)**.
   - **Master Scribe-Artist**: Illustrated on palm-leaves by **Kamalchandra (कमलचंद्र)**.
   - **Historical Status**: The **earliest dated illustrated manuscript** of Rajasthani painting discovered to date.
2. **Supasanahachariyam (सुपासनाहचरियं / पार्श्वनाथ चरित्र)**:
   - **Date & Location**: Executed in **1422–1423 CE** at **Delwara (Mewar)**.
   - **Patron Monarch**: Maharana **Mokal**.
   - **Master Artist**: Scribe-painter **Hirānanda (हीरानंद)**.
   - Shows the transition from Apabhramsha angularity to softer indigenous Rajput facial forms.

---

### 2.2 Udaipur Sub-style: The Golden Age of Sahibdin & Manohar
Under **Maharana Jagat Singh I (1628–1652 CE)**, Udaipur painting attained its zenith. Jagat Singh I established an official royal art studio within the Udaipur City Palace named:
> **"Chiteron ki Ovari" (चितेरों की ओवरी)**, popularly known across Rajputana as **"Tasveeraan ro Karkhano" (तस्वीराँ रो कारखानो)**.

#### The Twin Masters: Sahibdin & Manohar
- **Sahibdin (साहिबदीन)**: A master Muslim court artist deeply steeped in Hindu epics. He executed monumental narrative series:
  - *Ragamala Set* (1628 CE)
  - *Gitagovinda* of Jayadeva (1629 CE)
  - *Rasikapriya* of Keshavdas (1630 CE)
  - *Suryavansha* (1645 CE)
  - *Arsha Ramayana* (1648–1652 CE, specifically Yuddha Kanda and Sundar Kanda)
- **Manohar (मनोहर)**: A master Hindu contemporary who illustrated the *Bal Kanda* of the Ramayana in 1649 CE.
- **Visual Characteristics**:
  - Eyes shaped like fish (*Meenakshi* / मीनाक्षी).
  - Short, sturdy human statures; males wearing Mewari turbans (*Pheta*), waistbands (*Patka*), and *Gherdar Jama*.
  - Rich mineral colors: deep cinnabar red (*Hinglu*), brilliant saffron yellow (*Peedi*), lapis lazuli blue, and emerald green.
  - Distinctive vegetative motifs: lush **Kadamba tree (कदंब वृक्ष)** and stylized lotus ponds.

---

### 2.3 Chavand Sub-style (चावंड उपशैली)
- **Genesis**: Founded during the intense guerrilla resistance of **Maharana Pratap** after making Chavand his sovereign hill capital in **1585 CE**.
- **Golden Era**: Flourished under **Maharana Amar Singh I (1597–1620 CE)**.
- **The Chavand Ragamala (1605 CE)**: Master artist **Nasiruddin (Nisardi / निसारदीन)** painted the celebrated **Ragamala Set** at Chavand on **10 April 1605 CE**. It is considered the finest benchmark of pre-Mughal indigenous Rajput expressionism.

---

### 2.4 Nathdwara Sub-style: Pichhwai Art (नाथद्वारा उपशैली)
- **Historical Genesis**: Emerged after the sacred black marble idol of **Bhagwan Shrinathji** was transported from Govardhan (Braj) and permanently installed at **Sihad village (modern Nathdwara)** by **Maharana Raj Singh I in 1672 CE**.
- **Stylistic Synthesis**: A devotional blend of indigenous Mewari boldness and Braj (Vallabh/Pushtimarg) lyrical sweetness.

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │           THE ANATOMY OF PICHHWAI (पिछवाई कला)          │
                      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                                  │
          ┌───────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┐
          │                                       │                                       │
┌─────────┴─────────────┐               ┌─────────┴─────────────┐               ┌─────────┴─────────────┐
│  Spatial Function     │               │  Iconographic Motifs  │               │  Celebrated Masters   │
├───────────────────────┤               ├───────────────────────┤               ├───────────────────────┤
│ • Giant painted cloth │               │ • Shrinathji's Swarup │               │ • Male: Narottam,     │
│   screen hung behind  │               │ • Kamal Talai (Lilies)│   Ghasiram, Chaturbhuj│
│   the sanctum idol    │               │ • Holy Kamdhenu Cows  │ • **Women Artists**:  │
│ • Changes with seasons│               │ • Kadamba & Tamal boughs│  **Kamala & Ilaichi** │
└───────────────────────┘               └───────────────────────┘               └───────────────────────┘
```
- **Hallmark Characteristics**:
  - **Pichhwai (पिछवाई)**: Intricately painted cloth backdrops hung directly behind the idol of Shrinathji, changing according to the 8 daily *Jhankis* (worship rituals), festivals (Annakoot, Janmashtami, Radhashtami), and seasons (Sharad Purnima).
  - Prominent motifs: Blissful **cows of Braj (*Kamdhenu*)**, banana trees (*Kela*), Yamuna river cascades, and celestial aerial vehicles (*Vimana*).
  - **Celebrated Women Painters**: Nathdwara holds a unique distinction in Rajasthan's art history for its prominent master female painters: **Kamala (कमला)** and **Ilaichi (इलायची)**.

---

### 2.5 Devgarh Sub-style (देवगढ़ उपशैली)
- **Feudal Origin**: Developed in the first-class *Thikana* of Devgarh (Rajsamand), founded in 1680 CE by **Rawat Dwarkadas Chundawat** (a 16th Umrao of Mewar).
- **Discovery**: Brought to national and international academic recognition by art historian **Dr. Shridhar Andhare (डॉ. श्रीधर अंधारे)**.
- **Stylistic Fusion**: A unique blend of **Mewar, Marwar, and Dhundhar** styles.
- **Master Artists**: **Bagta (बगता)**, **Chokha (चोखा)**, and **Kavala (कवला)**.
- **Subject Matter**: Dynamic wild elephant fights (*Hathi ki Ladai*), raw royal boar hunts (*Shikar*), and courtly durbar ceremonies dominated by rich yellow-green palettes.

---8f:T31fa,Covering the vast arid expanses of Jodhpur, Bikaner, Kishangarh, Nagaur, and Jaisalmer, the Marwar School is distinguished by monumental scale, heroic expressions, radiant primary colors, and dramatic seasonal landscapes.

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │            MAJOR DIVISIONS OF THE MARWAR SCHOOL        │
                      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                                  │
          ┌───────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┐
          │                                       │                                       │

│  Jodhpur Sub-style    │               │  Kishangarh Style     │               │  Bikaner Sub-style    │
├───────────────────────┤               ├───────────────────────┤               ├───────────────────────┤

---

### 3.1 Jodhpur Sub-style (जोधपुर उपशैली)
- **Early Evolution**: Emerged under **Rao Maldeo (1531–1562 CE)**; showcased in the vibrant battle murals and celestial paintings of **Chokhelao Mahal (Mehrangarh Fort)** and the illustrated *Uttaradhyayana Sutra* (1591 CE).
- **Mughal Synthesis**: Initiated under Mota Raja Udai Singh and Maharaja Gaj Singh; refined under Maharaja Jaswant Singh I (*Barahmasa* and *Ragamala* sets).
- **The Golden Age of the Nath Sect**: Reached its unique zenith under **Maharaja Man Singh (1803–1843 CE)**. Inspired by his spiritual devotion to Ayas Devnath, Man Singh commissioned colossal illustrated sacred manuscripts:
  - *Nath Charitra*
  - *Shiva Purana*
  - *Durgacharit*
  - *Siddha Siddhanta Paddhati*
- **Visual Markers**:
  - Dominance of bright **yellow ochre (पीला रंग)**, scarlet red, and lapis blue.
  - Dramatic swirling, spiral monsoon clouds (*Ghumadte Badal*).
  - Tall, powerful male physiques wearing high pointed Marwari turbans (**Khidkiya Pagdi** / खिड़किया पगड़ी) and carrying shields and swords.
  - Almond-shaped eyes (*Badam si Aankhein*).
  - **Master Artists**: Amar Das, Bhati Shivdas, Dan Bhati, Shankar Das, Chhagan Das, Jeewan Das, and Ram Singh Bhati.

---

### 3.2 Kishangarh Sub-style: The Lyrical Zenith & Bani Thani
The Kishangarh school represents the absolute pinnacle of aristocratic romantic lyricism, mystical eroticism, and refined spiritual beauty in Indian art.

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │             THE PHENOMENON OF BANI THANI               │
                      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                                  │
          ┌───────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────┐
          │                                       │                                       │
┌─────────┴─────────────┐               ┌─────────┴─────────────┐               ┌─────────┴─────────────┐
│  The Royal Poet-Lover │               │  The Master Painter   │               │  Global Discovery     │
├───────────────────────┤               ├───────────────────────┤               ├───────────────────────┤
│ • Maharaja Savant     │               │ • **Moradhwaj Nihal   │               │ • **Eric Dickinson**  │
│   Singh (1748–1764)   │               │   Chand** (निहालचंद)  │ • Dr. Fayaz Ali       │
│ • Pen-name:           │               │ • Conceived Radha as  │ • Dubbed Bani Thani   │
│   **Nagari Das**      │               │   Bani Thani (1778 CE)│   **"Mona Lisa of     │
│ • Devoted to Vallabh  │               │ • Painted *Chandni    │   India"**            │
│   Bhakti at Vrindavan │               │   Raat ki Goshthi*    │ • 1973 Postal Stamp   │
└───────────────────────┘               └───────────────────────┘               └───────────────────────┘
```

#### 1. Historical & Romantic Backdrop
- **Maharaja Savant Singh (1748–1764 CE)**: A deeply spiritual Rathore prince and lyrical poet who composed devotional verses under the pseudonym **Nagari Das (नागरीदास)**.
- **Bani Thani (बणी-ठणी / Rasik Bihari)**: A singer, poetess, and consort of Sawai Savant Singh whose exquisite grooming, fashionable refinement, and spiritual beauty earned her the title *Bani-Thani* (The Well-Attired One). In their devotional imagination, Savant Singh visualized himself as Krishna and Bani Thani as Radha.
- In 1757 CE, Savant Singh abdicated his throne and retired with Bani Thani to the holy groves of **Vrindavan**, where both spent their remaining years in mystical contemplation.

#### 2. The Master Painter: Moradhwaj Nihal Chand (मोरध्वज निहाल चंद)
- Serving as the premier court painter from 1735 to 1757, Nihal Chand transformed the likeness of Bani Thani into the eternal, idealized archetype of the goddess **Radha**:
  - Extremely elongated, half-closed lotus-petal eyes curving upward toward the temples (**Khanjan Nayana** / खंजन नयन).
  - High, sharply arched brows.
  - A long, aristocratic, sharply pointed nose.
  - A delicate, protruding chin and serpentine locks of black hair caressing the cheek.
  - Draped in a diaphanous, translucent muslin veil (*Chunari / Odhani*).
  - Adorned with a delicate pearl nose-stud: the **Besari (बेसरी)** — the ultimate diagnostic ornament of Kishangarh painting!

#### 3. Global Inscription & Postal Stamp
- **Eric Dickinson & Dr. Fayaz Ali**: British scholar Eric Dickinson and Indian researcher Dr. Fayaz Ali brought Kishangarh art to international prominence in the 1940s. Dickinson famously christened Bani Thani as the **"Mona Lisa of India"** (*भारत की मोनालिसा*).
- **Government of India Postal Stamp**: On **5 May 1973**, the Indian Postal Department released a **20-paise commemorative postage stamp** featuring Nihal Chand’s portrait of Bani Thani.
- **Other Masterpieces & Painters**:
  - *Chandni Raat ki Sangeet Goshthi* (Music Party on a Moonlit Night) — painted by master artist **Amarchand (अमरचंद)**.
  - Other artists: Sitaram, Surdhwaj, Badan Singh, Nanakram, and Sawai Ram.

---

### 3.3 Bikaner Sub-style: Usta & Matheerna Heritage
- **Historical Genesis**: Developed under **Rao Bika** and accelerated during **Maharaja Rai Singh's** close alliance with Akbar.
- **Golden Age**: Reached peak maturity under **Maharaja Anup Singh (1669–1698 CE)**, who patronized royal ateliers and collected illustrated manuscripts (*Anup Sanskrit Library*).
- **The Unique Epigraphic Hallmark**: Unlike all other schools of Rajputana where artists remained anonymous, Bikaner artists **systematically inscribed their names, their father's name, their genealogy, and the precise date of completion** on the back of their paintings! The artists were given the respectful court title of **"Ustad" (उस्ताद)**.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   DUAL ARTISTIC HERITAGE OF BIKANER ART                                │
├────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ School / Technique         │ Operational Mechanics & Canonical Masters                 │
├────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ **1. Usta Art**            │ • Gilded relief work on treated **camel hide** and leather│
│ (उस्ता कला / मुनव्वती कला) │   casks (*Kuppi*), wooden ceilings, and marble.           │
│                            │ • Brought from Lahore by Rai Singh.                       │

│ (मथेरणा कला)**             │   of Bikaner** (*Matheerna caste*).                       │

│                            │   paintings, and wooden book cover paintings (*Patras*).  │
│                            │ • Masters: Munna Lal, Mukund, Chandu Lal, Ramlal.         │
└────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
- **Celebrated Ustad Artists**: Ruknuddin (रुकनुद्दीन), Ali Raza (अली रज़ा), Hamid, Isa, Hasan, and Abu Hamid.

---

### 3.4 Nagaur & Jaisalmer Sub-styles
- **Nagaur Sub-style**:
  - Reached its height under Maharaja Bakht Singh (1728–1751 CE).
  - Famous for **subdued, faint, chalky pastel colors (बुझे हुए रंग)**: pale terracotta, grey, and cream.
  - Delicate woodcut-like shading and remarkably sheer, transparent drapes on female figures.
- **Jaisalmer Sub-style**:
  - Uniquely celebrated as the **only painting school in Rajasthan that remained 100% immune to Mughal, British, or foreign influence**.
  - Patronized by Maharawal Akhai Singh and Moolraj II.
  - The universal, defining portraiture theme across Jaisalmer art is **Moomal (मूमल)** — the legendary princess of Lodharva.

---90:T17d8,Encompassing Amber, Jaipur, Alwar, Shekhawati, and Uniara, the Dhundhar School is characterized by close diplomatic ties with the Mughal court, monumental life-sized portraiture, opulent gold-leaf embellishments, and sprawling fresco murals.

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │            MAJOR DIVISIONS OF DHUNDHAR ART             │
                      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘

---

### 4.1 Amer & Jaipur Sub-styles

#### 1. Amer Sub-style (Early Phase)
- **Epoch**: Commenced during the reign of **Raja Man Singh I (1589–1614 CE)**.
- **Key Murals & Manuscripts**:
  - Murals at **Bharmal ki Chhatri (1599 CE)** and the garden pavilions of Amer Palace.
  - In 1588 CE, imperial artists at Amer illustrated the **Razmnama (रज्मनामा)** — the monumental Persian translation of the Mahabharata commissioned by Akbar (containing 169 miniatures).

#### 2. Jaipur Sub-style: The Suratkhana & Life-Sized Portraits
- **Sawai Jai Singh II (1700–1743 CE)**: Shifted the capital to Jaipur in 1727 and established **36 royal production ateliers (*Karkhanas*)**, including the dedicated painting studio named the **Suratkhana (सूरतखाना)**.
- **The Golden Age of Sawai Pratap Singh (1778–1803 CE)**: An ardent devotee of Krishna (*Brijnidhi*), Pratap Singh employed over 50 master artists in the Suratkhana, producing hundreds of paintings illustrating the Bhagavata Purana, Gitagovinda, and Ragamala.
- **The Master Painters**:
  1. **Sahibram (साहिबराम)**: The undisputed master of **monumental life-sized portraits (आदमकद चित्र / Aadmakad Chitra)**. He painted the famous life-sized standing portraits of Sawai Ishwari Singh, Sawai Madho Singh I, and Sawai Pratap Singh.
  2. **Mohammad Shah (मोहम्मद शाह)**: Famous for dynamic Krishna Lila depictions, court durbar scenes, and floral border arabesques.
- **Visual Characteristics**: Large fish-shaped eyes, soft round faces, extensive use of emerald green, ruby red, and liquid gold (*Halkari*), and rich jewel-inlay (*Moti-Panna Jadau*) work.

---

### 4.2 Alwar Sub-style (अलवर उपशैली)
- **Foundational Era**: Initiated when Rao Raja Pratap Singh established Alwar as an independent state in 1775 CE, bringing court painters Daluram and Saligram from Jaipur.
- **Golden Era of Maharaja Vinay Singh (1815–1857 CE)**:
  - Deeply patronized book illustrations and miniature art.
  - Commissioned the world-famous illustrated manuscript of Sheikh Saadi’s **Gulistan (गुलिस्तां)**, executed over decades by master artists **Baldev** and **Ghulam Ali** using real gold, pearl, and lapis lazuli pigments.
- **Two Unique Diagnostic Signatures**:
  1. **Miniature Paintings on Elephant Tusk / Ivory (हाथी दाँत के फलकों पर चित्रण)**: The only school in Rajasthan where artists perfected painting fine micro-miniatures directly onto polished elephant ivory sheets.
  2. **Portraits of Courtesans (*Veshyas / Ganikas* / वेश्याओं के चित्र)**: Alwar is unique among Rajput principalities for commissioning dedicated, respectful portrait studies of royal courtesans, nautch dancers, and female court musicians.
- **Master Artists**: Daluram, Baldev, Ghulam Ali, Saligram, Jamnadas, and Chhote Lal.

---

### 4.3 Shekhawati & Uniara Sub-styles
- **Shekhawati Sub-style**: Flourished as a wall-painting (*Fresco*) idiom rather than paper miniatures. Local painters (*Chiteras*) covered thousands of square meters of haveli walls with wet-plaster *Ala-Gila* murals, moving from mythological Krishna Lila scenes to depictions of British technology (steam locomotives, motorcars, and airplanes).
- **Uniara Sub-style**: Developed in the Uniara Thikana (Tonk), representing an exquisite cross-pollination between **Dhundhar and Hadoti** styles. Patronized by Rao Sardar Singh; renowned master artists include **Dheema (धीमा)**, **Mir Baksh (मीर बख्श)**, Kashi, and Ramlakhan.

---91:T1474,The Hadoti School, centered in the rugged gorges and verdant forests of the Chambal river basin (Bundi and Kota), is internationally recognized for its dynamic depiction of wild flora and fauna, monsoon squalls, and dramatic hunting expeditions.

```
                      ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                      │            DUAL SPECTRUM OF HADOTI PAINTING            │
                      └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                                  │
          ┌───────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────┐
          │                                                                               │
┌─────────┴─────────────────────────────┐                     ┌─────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
│  Bundi Sub-style                      │                     │  Kota Sub-style                          │
├───────────────────────┬───────────────┤                     ├─────────────────────────┬────────────────────────┤
│ • "School of Birds    │ • Chitrashala │                     │ • "School of the Royal  │ • Women depicted       │
│    and Animals"       │   (Rang Mahal)│                     │    Hunt" (*Shikar*)     │   hunting in jungles!  │
│ • Dense vegetation    │ • Monsoon rain│                     │ • Vallabh Sect devotion │ • Master: Dalu         │
│ • Lotus-filled pools  │   & peacocks  │                     │ • Extreme dynamism      │ • Ragamala (1768 CE)   │
└───────────────────────┴───────────────┘                     └─────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 5.1 Bundi Sub-style: The School of Birds & Animals
- **International Acclaim**: Celebrated globally as the **"School of Birds and Animals" (पशु-पक्षियों की चित्रशैली)** due to its unmatched intimacy with the natural world.
- **Landscape Anatomy**: Paintings are laden with dense jungle hills, cascading waterfalls, banyan and plantain trees, blossoming lotuses in stepped tanks, and vivid fauna (dancing peacocks, roaring tigers, caparisoned elephants, and water birds).
- **The Chitrashala / Rang Mahal of Bundi**:
  - Commissioned inside the Bundi Garh Palace by **Maharao Ummed Singh (1749–1770 CE)**.
  - Consists of world-famous continuous wall-to-ceiling fresco galleries depicting Krishna swinging with the Gopis, royal monsoon processions, and Rama’s coronation.
  - Famous as the **"Paradise of Murals"** (*भित्ति चित्रों का स्वर्ग*).
- **Color Palette & Lighting**: Bright red, emerald green, and golden yellow; famous for nocturnal scenes illuminated by flashes of lightning against inky black monsoon clouds (*Bijli ki Chamak*).
- **Master Artists**: Surjan (सुर्जन), Ahmad Ali (अहमद अली), Ramlal, Sadhu Ram, and Kishan.

---

### 5.2 Kota Sub-style: The School of the Royal Hunt (*Shikar*)
- **Historical Partition**: Originally an offshoot of Bundi art; emerged as an independent school under **Maharao Ram Singh I (1696–1707 CE)**.
- **Golden Era of Maharao Ummed Singh I (1770–1819 CE)**: Ummed Singh’s passion for big-game hunting in the dense ravines of the Chambal river elevated hunting imagery to high art.
- **The Supreme Hallmark — Women Hunting in Jungles**:
  - The single most distinguishing feature of Kota painting: **queens, royal princesses, and noblewomen are depicted actively hunting wild animals alongside kings**, riding galloping stallions or mounted on elephants, armed with matchlock guns, spears, and bows!
  - No other art tradition in India portrays royal women engaged in fierce wilderness combat with such power and frequency.
- **Pushtimarg Religious Fervor**: Deeply influenced by the Vallabh sect (Krishna as *Brajraj* and *Nathji*).
- **Master Artists & Masterpieces**:
  - Master artist **Dalu (डालू)** executed the celebrated **Kota Ragamala Set in 1768 CE** (the largest illustrated Ragamala manuscript in Hadoti, containing 36 miniatures).
  - Other master painters: Nuru Mohammad (नूर मोहम्मद), Lachhiram, Govindram, and Raghunath.

---93:T11a7,1. **The Pioneer of Scientific Classification**: **Dr. Anand Kentish Coomaraswamy** classified Rajasthani painting scientifically in his 1916 book **"Rajput Painting"**, NOT James Tod.
2. **"Rajput Painting" vs "Rajasthani Chitrasheili"**: Coomaraswamy coined *"Rajput Painting"*; **Rai Krishnadas** discarded dynastic titles and established the geographical term **"Rajasthani Chitrasheili"**.
3. **Earliest Dated Illustrated Manuscript**: **Shravaka Pratikramana Sutra Churni (1260 CE)**, painted by **Kamalchandra** at Ahar during Guhil King **Rawal Tejasimha's** reign, NOT Kumbha's reign.
4. **The "Chiteron ki Ovari" Founder**: Established in Udaipur City Palace by **Maharana Jagat Singh I** (1628–1652 CE), popularly known as **"Tasveeraan ro Karkhano"**.
5. **Sahibdin vs Sahibram Trap (Top RPSC Killer Trap!)**:
   - **Sahibdin (साहिबदीन)**: Master painter of the **Mewar School (Udaipur)** under Jagat Singh I (painted *Ragamala*, *Gitagovinda*, *Rasikapriya*, *Arsha Ramayana*).
   - **Sahibram (साहिबराम)**: Master painter of the **Dhundhar School (Jaipur)** under Ishwari Singh, Madho Singh, and Pratap Singh (pioneered **Aadmakad life-sized portraits**).
6. **The Chavand Ragamala Date & Artist**: Painted in **1605 CE** at Chavand by **Nasiruddin (Nisardi)** during the reign of **Maharana Amar Singh I**, NOT during Kumbha or Sanga.
7. **Pichhwai Fabric & Subject**: Pichhwai is painting executed on **cloth** (NOT paper or wood) hung behind the Shrinathji idol depicting Krishna Leela and Kamdhenu cows.
8. **Celebrated Women Painters of Rajasthan**:
   - **Kamala & Ilaichi**: Master painters of the **Nathdwara Sub-style (Mewar School)**.
   - **Sahiba (साहिबा)**: Female painter of the **Ajmer Sub-style (Marwar School)**.
9. **Devgarh School Discoverer**: Brought to light by art historian **Dr. Shridhar Andhare**; master painters were **Bagta, Chokha, and Kavala**.
10. **The "Mona Lisa of India" Coiner**: **Eric Dickinson** termed Bani Thani the "Mona Lisa of India", NOT Karl Khandalavala or Anand Coomaraswamy.
11. **Bani Thani Postal Stamp Details**: Issued on **5 May 1973** by the Government of India; denomination was **20 paise**.
12. **The Signature Diagnostic Ornament of Bani Thani**: The **Besari (बेसरी)** — a delicate pearl nose-ring/stud worn on the nose.
13. **"Chandni Raat ki Sangeet Goshthi" Artist**: Painted by **Amarchand (अमरचंद)** of the **Kishangarh School**, NOT Nihal Chand.
14. **The Only School Where Artists Signed Their Works**: **Bikaner Sub-style**; Muslim master artists titled **Ustad** inscribed their names, father's names, and dates (*Samvat*).
15. **Usta Art vs Matheerna Art**:
    - **Usta Art (Munawwati)**: Embossed gold work on **camel leather** (Hisam-ud-din Usta).
    - **Matheerna Art**: Traditional religious murals and wooden *Patra* paintings executed by the local **Jain community of Bikaner**.
16. **The School with "Muted / Chalky Colors"**: **Nagaur Sub-style** is characterized by faint, subdued, chalky pastel colors (*बुझे हुए रंग*).
17. **The 100% Indigenous, Uninfluenced School**: **Jaisalmer Sub-style** remained completely untouched by Mughal or British elements; its defining feminine portrait theme is **Moomal**.
18. **The Suratkhana of Jaipur**: Established by **Sawai Jai Singh II** as one of the 36 royal ateliers (*Karkhanas*); reached its zenith under **Sawai Pratap Singh**.
19. **Elephant Tusk Miniature Painting**: Exclusively practiced in the **Alwar Sub-style**, along with dedicated portraits of courtesans (*Ganikas*).
20. **Illustrated "Gulistan" Artists**: Master painters **Baldev and Ghulam Ali** illustrated Sheikh Saadi’s *Gulistan* for **Maharaja Vinay Singh of Alwar**.
21. **The "School of Birds and Animals"**: **Bundi Sub-style** is universally known as the *Pashu-Pakshiyon ki Chitrasheili*.
22. **The Chitrashala of Bundi Patron**: Built inside Garh Palace, Bundi by **Maharao Ummed Singh (1749–1770 CE)**; known as the *"Paradise of Murals"*.
23. **Women Depicted Hunting**: The exclusive hallmark of the **Kota Sub-style** — royal queens and princesses are depicted shooting lions and wild boars in the jungles.
24. **Kota Ragamala (1768 CE) Artist**: Executed by master artist **Dalu (डालू)**, comprising 36 miniatures.
25. **Uniara Sub-style Patron & Artists**: Sub-school of Dhundhar with Hadoti traits, patronized by Sardar Singh; artists were **Dheema, Mir Baksh, Kashi, and Ramlakhan**.

---94:T2e50,### 8.1 2-Markers (15–20 Words)

#### Q1: What is "Chiteron ki Ovari"?
**Answer**:
A royal painting studio established in Udaipur City Palace by Maharana Jagat Singh I (1628–1652), popularly called *"Tasveeraan ro Karkhano"*, marking the golden age of Mewar miniature painting.

---

#### Q2: Who gave Bani Thani the title "Mona Lisa of India", and who painted it?
**Answer**:
Painted in 1778 CE by master artist **Moradhwaj Nihal Chand** under patron-poet **Sawai Savant Singh (Nagari Das)**; christened the *"Mona Lisa of India"* by art scholar **Eric Dickinson**.

---

#### Q3: Name two prominent female painters of Rajasthani art and their sub-school.
**Answer**:
**Kamala** and **Ilaichi**, who flourished as master painters in the **Nathdwara Sub-style** (Mewar School), creating celebrated Shrinathji *Pichhwai* paintings.

---

#### Q4: Why is the Bikaner painting school considered unique in Rajasthan?
**Answer**:
Unlike other anonymous Rajput schools, Bikaner painters systematically inscribed their **names, their father's names, and precise completion dates** (*Samvat*) on the back of their artworks under the title *Ustad*.

---

#### Q5: State the defining stylistic characteristic of the Kota painting school.
**Answer**:
Dynamic wilderness hunting scenes (*Shikar*), featuring the unique portrayal of **royal women and queens actively hunting lions and wild boars** alongside kings in the Chambal ravines.

---

### 8.2 5-Markers (50 Words)

#### Q6: Analyze the thematic and artistic features of Pichhwai art of Nathdwara.
**Answer**:
Originating after Shrinathji's idol installation at Nathdwara (1672 CE) by Maharana Raj Singh I, **Pichhwai** is a sacred textile art tradition of the Pushtimarg sect:
1. **Material & Function**: Monumental paintings executed on cloth, suspended directly behind the sanctum idol to reflect the liturgical season or festival (*Annakoot*, *Sharad Purnima*).
2. **Iconography**: Centered on Shrinathji’s Govardhan Leela, flanked by sacred *Kamdhenu* cows, Kadamba trees, lotus ponds, and celestial Gopis.
3. **Master Artists**: Narottam, Ghasiram, and renowned female painters **Kamala and Ilaichi**.

---

#### Q7: Delineate the distinct artistic characteristics of the Kishangarh School of Painting.
**Answer**:
Flourishing under **Maharaja Savant Singh (Nagari Das)** and master artist **Moradhwaj Nihal Chand**, Kishangarh art represents lyrical romanticism:
1. **Facial Idealization**: Radha portrayed as **Bani Thani** with curved lotus eyes (*Khanjan Nayana*), arched brows, pointed chin, serpentine curls, and the signature pearl nose-ring (**Besari**).
2. **Atmospheric Settings**: Lyrical nocturnal landscapes, sprawling white marble terraces, Gundolav lake, and boating pageants (*Chandni Raat ki Goshthi* by Amarchand).
3. **Color Palette**: Dominated by pearl white, soft rose pink, shimmering gold, and azure blue.

---

#### Q8: Differentiate between Sahibdin and Sahibram in Rajasthan's painting traditions.
**Answer**:
Despite similar phonetics, they belong to entirely different schools, eras, and stylistic genres:
1. **Sahibdin (Mewar School)**: 17th-century court painter at Udaipur under Maharana Jagat Singh I; illustrated sacred epics (*Ragamala 1628*, *Gitagovinda 1629*, *Arsha Ramayana 1648*) with bright red/yellow mineral tones and fish-shaped eyes.
2. **Sahibram (Dhundhar/Jaipur School)**: 18th-century court painter at Jaipur under Sawai Ishwari Singh and Pratap Singh; pioneered monumental **life-sized portraits (Aadmakad Chitra)** using subtle shading and gem-inlay work.

---

#### Q9: "Rajasthani painting is not a monolithic art form, but a rich mosaic of regional schools reflecting distinct geographical landscapes, court cultures, and spiritual traditions." Critically examine.
**Answer**:
Rajasthani painting represents an extraordinary synthesis where regional geography, feudal politics, and religious movements molded distinct artistic idioms:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   REGIONAL MOSAIC OF RAJASTHANI PAINTING SCHOOLS                       │

│                           │ • Bikaner: Indo-Mughal courtly synthesis with dated Ustads.│
